q: (Only Allaah knows the correct meaning of these letters.)
v.s: Hā, Meem.
v.c: Ḥâ-Mĩm.

q: By the oath of the Clear Book
v.s: By the clear Book,
v.c: By the clear Book!

q: Verily We are the Ones Who warn
(people about the consequences of rejecting Imaan).
v.s: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were to warn [mankind].
v.c: Indeed, We sent it down on a blessed night, for We always warn ˹against evil˺.

q: decision of every matter of wisdom is passed on
v.s: Therein [i.e., on that night] is made distinct every precise matter -
v.c: On that night every matter of wisdom is ordained

q: (the duties of the angels for the forthcoming year are delegated to them on this night).
We are certainly the ones who send
v.s: [Every] matter [proceeding] from Us. Indeed, We were to send [a messenger]
v.c: by a command from Us, for We have always sent ˹messengers˺

q: ...by way of mercy from Us. He
is certainly All Hearing, All Knowing...
v.s: As mercy from your Lord. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing,
v.c: as a mercy from your Lord. He ˹alone˺ is truly the All-Hearing, All-Knowing—

q: ...The Rabb of the heavens, the earth and whatever is between the two.
v.s: Lord of the heavens and the earth and that between them, if you would be certain.
v.c: the Lord of the heavens and the earth and everything in between, if only you had sure faith.

q: There is no Ilaah but He Who gives life and death. He is your Rabb and the Rabb of your predecessors
v.s: There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death. [He is] your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers.
v.c: There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. He ˹alone˺ gives life and causes death. ˹He is˺ your Lord, and the Lord of your forefathers.

q: (instead of accepting the truth of Islaam)
(pleased to stick to their look of faith instead of submitting to the truth).
v.s: But they are in doubt, amusing themselves.
v.c: In fact, they are in doubt, amusing themselves.

q: (if they refuse to accept, let them)
(they will be struck with a severe drought and because of their intense hunger, it will appear to them as if)
the sky will issue forth a manifest smoke...
v.s: Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke
v.c: Wait then ˹O Prophet˺ for the day ˹when˺ the sky will be veiled in haze, clearly visible,

q: (This affected the people of Makkah when Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Muslims were already living in Madinah.)
v.s: Covering the people; this is a painful torment.
v.c: overwhelming the people. ˹They will cry,˺ “This is a painful torment.

q: from us and we will surely accept Imaan.”
(Hence, the Mushrikeen of Makkah pleaded to Rasulullaah ﷺ' to pray for rain and to request the leader of Yamaamah to supply them with grain.)
v.s: [They will say], "Our Lord, remove from us the torment; indeed, we are believers."
v.c: Our Lord! Remove ˹this˺ torment from us, ˹and˺ we will certainly believe.”

q: when a manifest Rasool has already come to them...
v.s: How will there be for them a reminder [at that time]? And there had come to them a clear Messenger.
v.c: How can they be reminded when a messenger has already come to them, making things clear,

q: ...and they turned away from him saying, “He is a trained madman”?
v.s: Then they turned away from him and said, "[He was] taught [and is] a madman."
v.c: then they turned away from him, saying, “A madman, taught by others!”?

q: while, but you people will certainly return
(to kufr and Shirk). (As the Qur'aan predicted, when the rains fell and the grain arrived, they broke their promise and continued living as Mushrikeen.)
v.s: Indeed, We will remove the torment for a little. Indeed, you [disbelievers] will return [to disbelief].
v.c: Indeed, We will remove ˹that˺ torment for a while, and you ˹Meccans˺ will return ˹to disbelief˺.

q: when We shall seize them with a firm grip
(when they will be punished and will find no escape).
v.s: The Day We will strike with the greatest assault, indeed, We will take retribution.
v.c: ˹Then˺ on the Day We will deal ˹you˺ the fiercest blow, We will surely inflict punishment.

q: Before them We had definitely tested the people of Fir'oun, to whom an honourable
v.s: And We had already tried before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger [i.e., Moses],
v.c: Indeed, before them We tested Pharaoh’s people: a noble messenger came to them,

q: ...(saying to Fir'oun) “(Release them from slavery and)
to me. I am a trustworthy Rasool
v.s: [Saying], "Render to me the servants of God. Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger,"
v.c: ˹proclaiming,˺ “Hand over the servants of Allah to me. I am truly a trustworthy messenger to you.

q: I have come to you with a clear proof
v.s: And [saying], “Be not haughty with God. Indeed, I have come to you with clear authority.
v.c: And do not be arrogant with Allah. I have certainly come to you with a compelling proof.

q: (However, Fir'oun refused to accept the message and when he threatened violence, Moosa ﵊ said,)
“I seek refuge with my Rabb and your Rabb against your harming me.”
v.s: And indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me.
v.c: And indeed, I seek refuge with my Lord and your Lord so you do not stone me ˹to death˺.

q: “If you will not believe me, then
(because if you attempt to harm me, Allaah will soon destroy you).”
v.s: But if you do not believe me, then leave me alone."
v.c: ˹But˺ if you do not believe me, then let me be.”

q: (However, despite repeated efforts to convince Fir'oun and his people to accept Imaan, they refused and continued harassing the Mu'mineen.)
prayed to his Rabb saying, “These people are certainly a sinful nation
v.s: And [finally] he called to his Lord that these were a criminal people.
v.c: Ultimately, he cried out to his Lord, “These are a wicked people!”

v.s: [God said], "Then set out with My servants by night. Indeed, you are to be pursued.
v.c: ˹Allah responded,˺ “Leave with My servants at night, for you will surely be pursued.

q: (Moosa ﵊ left with the Bani Israa'eel one night. When Fir'oun received news of this, he mustered a large army and set out in pursuit of the Bani Israa'eel. Allaah instructed Moosa ﵊ to strike the ocean with his staff, causing the waters to hold back and form several dry paths for them to cross over to the opposite shore. When the Bani Israa'eel went across, Fir'oun followed with his troops. Allaah addressed Moosa ﵊ saying,)
(so that Fir'oun and his army may enter it)
for they are an army who will be drowned
v.s: And leave the sea in stillness. Indeed, they are an army to be drowned."
v.c: And leave the sea parted, for they are certainly an army bound to drown.”

q: Plenty were the gardens and springs that they
v.s: How much they left behind of gardens and springs
v.c: ˹Imagine˺ how many gardens and springs the tyrants left behind,

v.s: And crops and noble sites
v.c: as well as ˹various˺ crops and splendid residences,

v.s: And comfort wherein they were amused.
v.c: and luxuries which they fully enjoyed.

q: We then made others successors to this
v.s: Thus. And We caused to inherit it another people.
v.c: So it was. And We awarded it ˹all˺ to another people.

q: Neither the sky nor the earth wept for them
(for the people of Fir'oun when they were destroyed),
(when the time for their destruction arrived,)
(any postponement because it was too late).
v.s: And the heaven and earth wept not for them, nor were they reprieved.
v.c: Neither heaven nor earth wept over them, nor was their fate delayed.

q: Undoubtedly We saved the Bani Israa'eel from the humiliating punishment...
v.s: And We certainly saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment -
v.c: And We certainly delivered the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment

q: ...of Fir'oun. He was certainly a haughty
(exceed the limits of humanity and morality).
v.s: From Pharaoh. Indeed, he was a haughty one among the transgressors.
v.c: of Pharaoh. He was truly a tyrant, a transgressor.

q: We granted superiority to the Bani Israa'eel over the
v.s: And We certainly chose them by knowledge over [all] the worlds.
v.c: And indeed, We chose the Israelites knowingly above the others.

q: And We gave them such Aayaat
(demonstrating Our power, like the splitting of the sea)
in which there was clear grace
(many blessings which served to strengthen their Imaan).
v.s: And We gave them of signs that in which there was a clear trial.
v.c: And We showed them signs in which there was a clear test.

v.s: Indeed, these [disbelievers] are saying,
v.c: Indeed, these ˹Meccans˺ say,

q: is merely our first death and we will not be resurrected
v.s: "There is not but our first death, and we will not be resurrected.
v.c: “There is nothing beyond our first death, and we will never be resurrected.

v.s: Then bring [back] our forefathers, if you should be truthful."
v.c: Bring ˹back˺ our forefathers, if what you say is true.”

q: (Despite the immense strength of these people,)
We destroyed them all, for they were all sinners
v.s: Are they better or the people of Tubbaʿ and those before them? We destroyed them, [for] indeed, they were criminals.
v.c: Are they superior to the people of Tubba’ and those before them? We destroyed them ˹all˺, ˹for˺ they were truly wicked.

q: We have not created the heavens, the earth and whatever is between the two in vain
(there are definite reasons for the creation of everything).
v.s: And We did not create the heavens and earth and that between them in play.
v.c: We did not create the heavens and the earth and everything in between for sport.

q: We have created them with wisdom
but most people do not know
(that the same Allaah Who created the whole of creation can easily resurrect them on the Day of Qiyaamah).
v.s: We did not create them except in truth, but most of them do not know.
v.c: We only created them for a purpose, but most of these ˹pagans˺ do not know.

q: Indeed, the Day of Judgement has been stipulated for all of them.
v.s: Indeed, the Day of Judgement is the appointed time for them all -
v.c: Surely the Day of ˹Final˺ Decision is the time appointed for all—

q: The day when one companion will be of no benefit to another, neither shall they be assisted...
v.s: The Day when no relation will avail a relation at all, nor will they be helped -
v.c: the Day no kith or kin will be of benefit to another whatsoever, nor will they be helped,

q: ...But those on whom Allaah has mercy. Allaah is undoubtedly the Mighty, the Most Merciful.
v.s: Except those [believers] on whom God has mercy. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
v.c: except those shown mercy by Allah. He is truly the Almighty, Most Merciful.

v.s: Indeed, the tree of zaqqūm
v.c: Surely ˹the fruit of˺ the tree of Zaqqûm

v.s: Is food for the sinful.
v.c: will be the food of the evildoer.

q: It will be like the residue of oil
v.s: Like murky oil, it boils within bellies
v.c: Like molten metal, it will boil in the bellies

v.s: Like the boiling of scalding water.
v.c: like the boiling of hot water.

q: (Allaah will command the angels of punishment)
him to the very midst of the Blazing Fire!”
v.s: [It will be commanded], "Seize him and drag him into the midst of the Hellfire,
v.c: ˹It will be said,˺ “Seize them and drag them into the depths of the Hellfire.

q: “Then pour the punishment of boiling water over his head.”
v.s: Then pour over his head from the torment of scalding water."
v.c: Then pour over their heads the torment of boiling water.”

q: (the ones who regarded yourself as the)
(in the world and therefore refused to accept the message of the Ambiyaa)
v.s: [It will be said], “Taste! Indeed, you are the honoured, the noble!
v.c: ˹The wicked will be told,˺ “Taste this. You mighty, noble one!

q: is what you used to doubt.”
(Now you have in it in front of you and cannot doubt anything.)
v.s: Indeed, this is what you used to dispute."
v.c: This is truly what you ˹all˺ used to doubt.”

q: Verily those with Taqwa shall be in a place of peace...
v.s: Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure place:
v.c: Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure place,

v.s: Within gardens and springs,
v.c: amid Gardens and springs,

q: They will wear clothing of fine silk and thick silk, and will be seated facing each other
v.s: Wearing [garments of] fine silk and brocade, facing each other.
v.c: dressed in fine silk and rich brocade, facing one another.

q: This is how it will be. We will also marry them to fair, large-eyed damsels.
v.s: Thus. And We will marry them to fair women with large, [beautiful] eyes.
v.c: So it will be. And We will pair them to maidens with gorgeous eyes.

q: In comfort, they will call for all types of fruit there
v.s: They will call therein for every [kind of] fruit - safe and secure.
v.c: There they will call for every fruit in serenity.

q: They will not taste death there, but for the first death
(of this world which would have already passed).
Allaah will save them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire...
v.s: They will not taste death therein except the first death, and He will have protected them from the punishment of Hellfire
v.c: There they will never taste death, beyond the first death. And He will protect them from the punishment of the Hellfire—

q: ...as a favour from your Rabb. This is the greatest success
v.s: As bounty from your Lord. That is what is the great attainment.
v.c: as ˹an act of˺ grace from your Lord. That is ˹truly˺ the ultimate triumph.

v.s: And indeed, We have eased it [i.e., the Qur’ān] in your tongue that they might be reminded.
v.c: Indeed, We have made this ˹Quran˺ easy in your own language ˹O Prophet˺ so perhaps they will be mindful.

v.s: So watch, [O Muhammad]; indeed, they are watching [for your end].
v.c: Wait then! They too are certainly waiting.
